$comment: THE PRODUCT'S NUMBERS, IN ONE PLACE.
Every value here is written by hand in several other files: the copy
catalogue, the worker's message templates, the terms of use, the billing
FAQ and the legal brief. That duplication is not going away — a price in
`termos-de-uso.md` has to be prose, not a placeholder, because it is a
contract clause — so the answer is not to generate those files but to be
able to prove they still agree. `apps/web/lib/product.test.ts` does that:
it fails, naming the file, when any of them drifts from this one.
Why it exists: D11b was three hardcoded dates, D7 was one claim in four
places, D6 survived a guard that keyed on the wrong phrasing. Each was a
product fact typed by hand in more places than anyone could hold in their
head, and each was found by a person reading one screen closely.
Changing a number here does NOT change what renders. It changes the test
from green to red, listing every site still carrying the old value.
Money is in whole BRL. Dates are ISO, in the product's clock
(America/Sao_Paulo) — see CLAUDE.md on the three clocks.

$seatsComment: Two numbers, because the offer opens in two lots and they are not the
`seatsTotal` (25) is CONTRACTUAL — terms §6 says the offer is limited to
25 subscribers, released in lots of 17 and then 8. Changing it changes a
`seatsOpenDefault` (17) is only the value a fresh database starts at.
**The live cap is a row in `app_settings`, not this file.** Opening lot 2
must be an UPDATE, never a deploy: releasing eight seats should not
require a CI run, an image build and a redeploy, and on 2026-09-26 that
chain took six days to complete once.
The invariant the code enforces: the cap may be raised freely, and
lowered only to a value at or above the highest seat already assigned.
Lowering it past an assigned seat would push somebody out of an offer
A seat is RESERVED, not bought. Reserving costs nothing and happens now;
the charge starts on 17/10 when the plan opens. So `seat` on
`founders_list` records a booking, and a subscription is a separate
thing that does not exist yet (E8). Sci opens lot 2 only if the 17 are
still not taken by 17/10 — a decision, never a schedule.

$planLimitsComment: THE QUOTA NUMBERS THE COPY SELLS. NOT THE RUNTIME AUTHORITY.
`plan_limits` stays the table the product reads at request time —
TECHNICAL_SPEC.md:302 calls it 'configurable without a deploy' and :475
says 'Numbers live in `plan_limits`, not in code'. **No quota decision**
reads what is here — a route that renders copy does, through messages.ts,
but only to print a sentence — and no `readLimit` call was replaced by a
constant. Raising Básico from 5 to 8 is still one UPDATE.
What this is: the **stated** value. Three rows are sold word-for-word in
about a dozen pt-BR strings and in the terms' entitlement table, and until
D69 nothing compared the sentence to the row. D64 removed the last
incidental assertions (literals inside route-contract suites), so a
migration lowering Básico to 3 was silent while every page kept promising
five. CDC art. 30 binds an advertised feature, so the sentence is a
promise, not a label.
Keyed `(plan, feature)` — the table's own primary key, spelled the same
way — so the two sides can be joined by eye as well as by a test. The
`period` is here because `month` versus `total` is the difference between
'five a month' and 'five for life', and a quantity without its period is
half a fact.
Only the rows the copy quotes. `deep_analysis`, `alert`, `keywords`,
`states` and `price_band` are also sold in sentences, and exactly **one**
of them has a real copy-versus-table guard: `keyword-limits.db.test.ts`,
which walks the catalogue and compares each claimed number to the row.
`plan-limits.db.test.ts` is **not** one — it asserts the table against
literals (`toBe(1)`, `period === 'week'`) and reads no copy at all, so
`alert` is covered only incidentally. All four of the others, price_band
included, are card D74.
A row added here must be tokenised in the catalogue and swept in the same
PR, or the guard grows a hole it cannot see — and `product.db.test.ts`
asserts this list **exactly**, so adding one without doing the rest goes
red rather than quiet.
Three readers: `apps/web/lib/product.ts` (PLAN_LIMITS, which feeds the
`{$triagensVisitante}`, `{$diasVisitante}` and `{$triagensBasico}` copy
tokens), `product.test.ts` (the catalogue and the terms must still say
this) and `product.db.test.ts` (the table must still hold it).

notice.$noticeComment: priceChangeDays is the CONTRACTUAL FLOOR (terms §6.4), not the operating value. Sending earlier is always allowed; later never is.

$refundComment: Terms §8 and faq-cobranca. Days 1-7 are CDC art. 49 — full refund, no
deduction, and it wins whenever both windows apply. Days 8-30 are our own
guarantee and return the amount paid minus the acquirer's processing fee.
The net figure quoted in the copy (R$ 55,08) is NOT stored: it is
promocional - processingFeeBrl, and product.test.ts asserts the prose
still matches that subtraction. A number written down twice is a number
that drifts; a number derived once cannot.
